name: Clyde Starr
life: “I still remember a child picking the least showy costume in the box.” Sunday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Clyde usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I bought the child a costume for the school play. He wants his brother in the audience more than he wants a crown.
appearance: Clyde is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Usually dressed in a mustard canvas overshirt with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip, Clyde rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
personality: Clyde has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To get the older brother into the audience.
family: Vincent Albright is Clyde’s older relative by marriage. Clyde makes room at the table. Vincent brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The other side of the cove*, Vincent says, “I object to putting people's names on benches.”
connections: Jody Dunn. A school play gives another dealer a concrete reason to cover for a brother who needs to attend.

reactions.situation: His younger brother asks what he delivers for a living
reactions.response: Clyde lets the older brother choose honest words the younger boy can understand.

reactions.response: Clyde offers to accompany the caller to a familiar public meeting place without turning speculation into neighborhood news.
